items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: There was a white fellow named Tom McVey who called all the negro boys 'nigger' and he wanted to say something to me.

ctx.x: On a farm across from where we lived were two white boys and they had a pony and buggy. They drove to and from their school which was on the same road that Tom had to take, and when I first came there, Tom told me that these two boys would beat him up at times when they caught him coming home. I told him that I would meet him on the road one day and straighten the matter out. Eventually these two boys came along and when they saw Tom with someone larger than he was they must have figured something was going to…

Once when I was 12 years old, I had come to Centerville for the summer and as most of the boys worked helping with the harvest, I went to work also with a group thrashing wheat. I was what was known as a "jumper," which means the one on the wagon who stacks the wheat when it is thrown up from the ground. One day the thrasher machine broke down and everybody was lagging around waiting until it was repaired. There was a white fellow named Tom McVey who called all the negro boys "nigger" and he wanted to say…

of 24 years old at least. I was sitting on a wagon and he was laying on the ground chewing on a straw. I heard him when he called me nigger but I pretended not to hear him. He pointed his finger at me and said "Hey! you nigger," and I pointed my finger right back at him and told him that my name was William Johnson Coleman and if he could not call me one of those names, not to say anything to me. His face turned cherry red but he didn't move and I never knew what he wanted to say to me.
